subject: general
question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground, which is 48m away from the foot of the tower is 30°. Find the height of the tower.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°-60°-90° triangle**, the ratio of sides opposite to these angles is **1 : √3 : 2**.

Side opposite to **60°** (Base) = 48 m.

√3 units = 48 m ⇒ 1 unit = 48/√3 m.

Height (side opposite to 30°) = 1 unit = 16√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 16√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance from foot (Base) = 48 m, Angle of elevation (θ) = 30°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62ffbb8086373dc2027301202c8e8181a2aef55ca02672d5f0d2547c9a87fdc9.png] 

⇒ tan 30° = h / 48

⇒ 1/√3 = h / 48

⇒ h = 48 / √3

⇒ h = (48 × √3) / (√3 × √3)

⇒ h = 48√3 / 3 = 16√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 16√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation from an observer's eye to an object above is equal to the angle of depression from the object to the observer due to alternate interior angles.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².</p
